text:
Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently cruising towards victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday, this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition.
It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres. But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, with the German side having to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember. A frustrated Arteta will know his side must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight.
While Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri – on loan at Dortmund from the Gunners – had to make do with a place on their respective benches, the exploits of another teenager were on the Arsenal supporters’ lips on their way to the ground. A stunning solo goal from 14-year-old Luis Muñoz – an England Under-15 international who is the youngest player ever to feature in the Uefa Youth League – against Dortmund earlier in the day showed that Arsenal’s conveyor belt of talent continues to produce.
Aside from Myles Lewis-Skelly – a relative veteran these days at 20 – Arteta opted for experience as he made six changes from the draw against Newcastle on Saturday, including Kepa Arrizabalaga deputising in goal for the injured David Raya.
Dortmund haven’t been crowned German champions since Jürgen Klopp’s days in 2012 but lead the Bundesliga by two points from Bayern Munich. Like Arsenal, Niko Kovac’s side has relied on a solid defence and the Croatian manager attempted to stiffen his midfield by selecting Joey Veerman alongside Jobe Bellingham and ahead of their exciting Greece teenager, Konstantinos Karetsas.
Arrizabalaga had only started once this season, in the Carabao Cup win over Ipswich, and the Spain goalkeeper was largely a spectator again for the first 20 minutes as Arsenal assumed control. Christos Tzolis had two early sighters after being set up by the rejuvenated Noni Madueke but the Dortmund goalkeeper, Gregor Kobel, still seemed surprised by the power with which Gyökeres struck the ball in the 10th minute when he was fed by the England forward.
He was only introduced in the fourth minute of stoppage time against Newcastle as Arsenal chased a winner but scored an excellent goal in the victory over Slavia Prague three weeks ago and clearly had a point to prove as his shot arrowed into the back of the net from outside the area.
Kobel managed to get a hand to a Tzolis effort that was heading for the top corner soon after, although Madueke should really have doubled Arsenal’s lead on the rebound. Dortmund eventually managed to create some pressure at the other end when Fábio Silva fired over. But despite the best efforts of Bellingham and Felix Nmecha, they just could not sustain any meaningful possession against the dominance of Declan Rice and Lewis-Skelly.
A marauding run from the latter straight through the heart of Dortmund’s defence almost resulted in a second after a brilliant touch from Gyökeres. You began to wonder if Arsenal’s profligacy might cost them again when Arrizabalaga was finally called into action on the stroke of half-time after a rare mistake from Rice but he managed to push Julian Ryerson’s shot out for a corner.
Arteta had more cause for concern at the start of the second half when the Dortmund supporters behind Arsenal’s goal thought they should have had a penalty after a corner struck Gyökeres on the wrist but the Italian referee waved away their protests. There were groans at the other end when Martin Ødegaard passed up the opportunity to shoot after more good work from Madueke.
That was made to look even more costly when Dortmund equalised with their next attack. The outstanding Joane Gadou stepped out of defence brilliantly to play in Beier and he made no mistake with his left foot. Piero Hincapié then saw his header saved at the near post by Kobel. Clearly fancying his chances of a shock victory, Kovac threw on Karetsas and Serhou Guirassy as Arteta made a triple substitution. But Jurriën Timber’s first act was to give the ball away, with Bellingham only denied moments later by the assistant’s flag.
The Dortmund goal led a charmed life in the final 20 minutes as Arsenal piled on the pressure. Only Guirassy will know how the ball managed to strike the post twice in the space of a second as he attempted to clear from a clever Ødegaard free-kick. Rice couldn’t believe his luck when his effort struck the post again with Kobel well beaten. But Dortmund stuck to their task admirably and Arsenal had to learn the hard way again.
digest_he:
ארסנל שמטה יתרון ביתי פעם נוספת בתוך ארבעה ימים, כאשר בורוסיה דורטמונד המרשימה חילצה ממנה תיקו 1-1. ויקטור גיוקרס העלה את התותחנים יתרון במחצית הראשונה בבעיטה אדירה מחוץ לרחבה, אך הקבוצה הגרמנית השוותה במחצית השנייה משער של מקס בייר.

המשחק כלל החמצות רבות מצד ארסנל בדקות הסיום, כולל פגיעות רבות במסגרת השער, ופסילת שער דרמטי של ג'וב בלינגהאם בטענת נבדל. המאמן מיקל ארטטה יידרש לשיפור לקראת המפגש הבא מול ריאל מדריד.
